subject.title: Add optional `name`/`label` field to group config entries

question: Should OpenClaw add a canonical inert metadata field to opaque-ID group/channel entries, and should that field be named `label` rather than `name` or `description`?
rationale: The source proves the capability is absent but cannot establish the intended public config vocabulary or whether readable-key channel entries should receive the same field.

options.title: Adopt `label` for opaque IDs
options.body: Add an optional inert `label` string only to group/channel entries whose keys are stable opaque identifiers, with schema, metadata, docs, and round-trip coverage.

options.title: Apply one field everywhere
options.body: Add the chosen metadata property uniformly to every group and channel entry schema for maximum consistency.

options.title: Use discovery tooling only
options.body: Keep behavior-only schemas and instead improve directory or config tooling that maps stable IDs to live display names.

recommendation.title: Adopt `label` for opaque IDs
recommendation.body: Add an optional inert `label` string only to group/channel entries whose keys are stable opaque identifiers, with schema, metadata, docs, and round-trip coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: His recent merged history spans the central schema and multiple affected channel contracts, making him the strongest available owner for this cross-channel config decision.
